blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §12.3 fault_rate applicability

steps.claim: F_B is the lifted-oracle result. Actions, including permutation actions, have no fault outcome, while the certificate schema places a required fault_rate field on every region record.
The proposed text requires counts to be recomputed from F_B and requires context records for a scheduled region without restricting either rule to oracles.

The published controlled-action certificate contains two perm_action region records with empty fault maps. Adding the proposed invocation fields still supplies no F_B for either region; an independent checker would need to invent an action recount convention or refuse the requested recount.
The amended universal recount requirement is therefore not implementable for an existing legal certificate class without an additional normative applicability rule.

blocking.fix: In §12.3, make the field 'fault_rate: <oracle recount record> | null' and state: 'F_B recounts and fault_rate_contexts apply only to regions of kind oracle. For action and perm_action, fault_rate MUST be null and fault_rate_contexts MUST be absent. This denotes no action-owned fault outcome; it does not assert that nested oracle invocations are fault-free. Nested oracle recounts retain their own invocation/context bindings.' The corrected controlled-action fixture has fault_rate:null on both perm_action records. Alternatively, retain an explicitly defined empty action placeholder that is never evaluated through F_B and never discharges a callee obligation; I recommend null because it distinguishes inapplicability from a verified zero-fault recount.

blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §12.3 exclusion accounting; supporting claim of existing validation
blocking.problem: The premise 'existing independently validated exclusion classes' is unsupported by the cited ISA text. §12.3 only names undefined_excluded and layout_dependent_excluded; §§12.1–12.2 and 14.1 do not define classification evidence, its invocation/domain binding, or an independent exclusion-validation procedure. The proposed 'enumerated applicable domain count' also leaves unclear whether excluded tuples remain in the F_B recount. North Star §5.1 excludes these inputs from native comparison while retaining reference validation. This finding concerns the proposal's false claim of existing coverage, not a demand to redesign unrelated accepted text.
blocking.fix: Replace that language in §12.3 with: 'faults_by_code counts nonzero code(F_B) over every element of the declared §12.2 domain. Native-comparison exclusions do not remove elements from this reference recount. Exclusion counters MUST be independently reproduced from classification evidence bound to the same materialized program, invocation and domain. The default validation procedure replays the identified classifiers and input mapping over that domain. Missing replayable classification evidence makes the exclusion report unchecked and discharges no exclusion-dependent acceptance obligation; it MUST NOT be interpreted as zero exclusions.' State in the note that ISA 0.9 currently provides the counter names, not this validation contract. For example, if 64 of the witness's 256 tuples are independently classified as undefined, B=1 still reports faults_by_code={"1":"256"}, with undefined_excluded=64 separately. Alternatively, explicitly identify exclusion validation as an unresolved dependent contract and limit this repair's verification claim to the full-domain F_B recount; I recommend adding the obligation and default procedure here.

suggestions: In §12.3, clarify the intrinsic meaning of a contextual rate: 'A fault-rate domain is the underlying oracle's §5.2 domain. Inherited controls do not add domain components or suppress intrinsic code(F_B) counts. These counts are not probabilities of reaching the call from the root.' Thus placing the B=1 witness behind a disabled control does not turn its intrinsic 256 failures into zero.

In §12.3, replace 'reached' with 'present in the complete §12.1 invocation tree, including default-covered and predicated-off invocations'. For an action containing two calls to the same oracle, both contexts require records even when only one has explicit schedule entries.

In §15, add certificate-level acceptance vectors stating: 'Missing invocation, mismatched context invocation, duplicate or omitted context records, and an inconsistent legacy projection reject; equal token tuples with different process-local ids produce the same recount.' Keep the existing disclosure that arithmetic verification alone does not execute these certificate checks.
path_to_accept: 1. Restrict F_B recounts to oracles and define an explicit non-applicable representation for actions. 2. Remove the false assertion of existing exclusion validation; define full-domain reference counting and either add the independent classification obligation/default or explicitly identify that dependent contract as unresolved. Preserve the proposed invocation bindings, canonical context projection and migration rule.
summary: The central defect, clause references, two-budget witness and unchanged non-certificate hash claims check out. The proposal needs two contract corrections: action applicability and its unsupported assumption about exclusion validation. No core semantic change is needed.
